authorReviewNote: Quiver holds arrows. Bowstrings only/target faces/scorecards not its purpose. Actual World Archery manual section9.8 explicitly safe arrow storage and several quiver styles. Does not restrict it to worn-at-hip type; familiar equipment terminology and grammar sound.

Fletching stabilises arrow flight, not carrying bow, measuring distance or finger protection. Manual actual arrow-fletching discussion explicitly stability/flight; not inferred from table of contents. Helping qualifier permits drag and visibility as additional functions.

Armguard covers forearm against string. Finger tab protects fingers, quiver stores arrows and sight aids aim. Actual manual forearm-protection paragraph checked. No technique instruction or claim all accidental contact is impossible.

Gold at centre of standard five-colour target. Blue/black/white outside, red/yellow alternative not offered. Manual glossary explicitly gold central scoring colour; standard target scope avoids field-archery black/white faces. Colour naming handles gold/yellow convention.

String drawn back, unlike sight/grip/arrow-rest hardware. Manual full-draw definition and draw-string paragraphs inspected. Does not say every archer uses unaided fingers, allowing release aids and adapted techniques. Clear beginner fact.

Olympic weapon set foil/epee/sabre, other offered groups contain non-Olympic-fencing implements. FIE actual three-weapon descriptions inspected, not athlete roster. Épée accented correctly; no assertion these are all historical sword types.

Competition strip piste, not crease/rink/fairway. British Fencing referee-education actual field-of-play section checked; FIE also uses pistes. No mixed skiing ambiguity because sport explicit. Does not ask changing strip dimensions.

Mask covers face/head. Plastron torso, glove hand, shin guard legs. British Fencing actual equipment guidance explicitly mask requirements checked; not claiming all face guards from other sports qualify. Plain singular grammar.

Sabre scores edge and tip; foil/epee thrust tip, so all-three equally wrong. FIE actual weapon paragraph explicitly cutting-edge distinction inspected. No dated target-area or electronic-timing rule embedded.

Rewrote purpose-of-salute inference into documented pre-bout etiquette. British Fencing actual beginner-competition guide explicitly saluting opponent/officials before bout. Other offered actions not standard etiquette. No unsupported claim salute changes score or is optional.

Curling on ice, not sand/grass/clay. World Curling actual introduction and sheet description checked. Does not confuse dry-floor adaptations with standard sport. Basic accessible rule, no archived team-size assumption.

Target house, other options are actual different curling features hog-line/free-guard-zone/hack. World Curling actual house definition checked. Replaced duplicate crease/crease-line distractors. Not claiming entire sheet is the house.

Brushes/brooms sweep, not hockey stick/racket/golf club. World Curling actual equipment paragraph explicitly own brush. Scoped standard team curling because wheelchair curling has no sweeping. No oversimplified melting/friction physics claim.

End is round of stone delivery, not handle/tournament winner/training. World Curling actual End-a-round passage checked. No incorrect fixed16stones assertion for mixed doubles, since draft avoids quantity. Round phrasing clear.

Skip directs tactics, coxswain/wicketkeeper/libero other sports roles. Actual World Curling skip direct-play paragraph checked. Normally permits vice-skip takeover while skip delivering and skip not necessarily throwing fourth. No unsupported captain-only rule.

Return must front wall before floor, can first touch side/back wall. Actual current World Squash6.2.2 explicitly front-wall return without floor bounce. Other offered walls alone insufficient. Did not incorrectly demand direct front-wall-only stroke.

Replaced unsupported rubber-material candidate. Current World Squash6.2.1 requires return before ball bounces twice: at most once permitted, volley also allowed. Other counts/no-bounce-required wrong. Wording how many may normally bounce means maximum allowance, not mandatory one bounce; final prompt should make maximum explicit.

Let replays rally, not two points/end match/new racket. Current World Squash official-call glossary LET/PLAY A LET and YES LET explicitly replay. Referee's call qualifier distinguishes merely appealing unsuccessfully for let. No promise all interference wins let.

One foot floor-contact inside service box at hit. Actual current World Squash5.7.2 inspected, foot must not touch boundaries. Reworded to avoid ambiguous touching box line. Other sport centre-circle/goal-area/penalty-spot not squash serving position.

Tin low full-width front-wall area. Current World Squash glossary exact floor-to-lowest-horizontal-line definition checked. Net/crossbar/backboard different fixtures, not tin. No claim whole front wall is out.

Badminton singles one player per side. Actual BWF definitions inspected in federation-hosted official law PDF. Two/three/four not singles. Standard scope avoids team-tie totals; not inverse duplicate of old which-sport-uses-shuttlecock fact.

Changed pair-size giveaway to total doubles participants: four. BWF two players on each opposing side gives four, alternatives two/three/six wrong. No stem revealing numerical answer. Team tournament substitutes excluded by on-court wording.

Net separates badminton sides, not wall/channel/hurdles. Actual BWF court/net sections inspected. Does not ask borderline net fault mechanics. Standard match context clear and four choices grammatically parallel.

Stringed racket strikes shuttle; stringless paddle/club/curved stick wrong badminton equipment. BWF racket stringed-area and stroke definitions inspected. Distinct from identifying sport by shuttlecock, though same sport. No unnecessary equipment dimensions trivia.

Relevant boundary lines count in. Actual BWF law says all lines part of area they define, inspected. Out/automatic let/service fault wrong, standard whether singles/doubles/service court relevance explicitly qualified. Contact with line alone not fault.
